A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

protein kinase C and calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II are involved in the modulation of presynaptic Ca2+ channels in mouse brain nerve endings, whereas protein kinase C and Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinases are involved in the regulation of presynaptic K+ channels.
protein kinases are not involved in the modulation of presynaptic Na+ channels but they are involved in the modulation presynaptic Ca2+ channels.
the activation of presynaptic voltage-gated Na+ channels by veratridin is not modulated by protein kinases, but it is affected by drugs that interfere with Ca2+ dependent mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modulation of presynaptic Ca2+ channels by Ca2+ and protein kinase II may be an important mechanism in the regulation of neurotransmitter release.
the modulation of voltage sensitive Ca2+/Na+ channels is not mediated by protein kinases, but by other mechanisms.

, the modulation of voltage-sensitive Na+ channels is not a common feature among protein kinases, but rather a specific function of a particular kinase, i.e., Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II, in the case of presynaptic Ca2+ channels.
